Cognitive analytic therapy (CAT) is a form of psychological therapy initially developed in the United Kingdom by [Anthony Ryle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Ryle).

Cognitive anthropology is a subfield of [anthropology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthropology) influenced by [linguistic anthropology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linguistic_anthropology), [cultural anthropology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cultural_anthropology), and [biological anthropology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biological_anthropology) in which scholars seek to explain patterns of shared knowledge, [cultural](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cultural) [innovation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Innovation), and transmission over time and space using the methods and [theories](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theories) of the [cognitive sciences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cognitive_sciences) (especially [experimental psychology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Experimental_psychology) and [cognitive psychology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cognitive_psychology)) often through close collaboration with historians, [ethnographers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethnography), archaeologists, linguists, [musicologists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Musicology), and other specialists engaged in the description and [interpretation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interpretation_(logic)) of cultural forms.

Cognitive anthropology of symbolic systems is an interdisciplinary field that examines how human beings create, transmit, and interpret symbolic structures in relation to universal cognitive mechanisms and recurrent patterns found in nature.

Cognitive appraisal (also called simply 'appraisal') is the subjective [interpretation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interpretation_(logic)) made by an individual to [stimuli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stimulus_(physiology)) in the environment.
Cognitive archaeology is a [theoretical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archaeological_theory) perspective in [archaeology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archaeology) that focuses on the ancient mind.

Cognitive behavioral training (CBTraining), sometimes referred to as structured cognitive behavioral training (SCBT) is an organized process that uses systematic, highly-structured tasks designed to improve [cognitive functions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cognitive_skill).
Cognitive bias in animals is a pattern of deviation in judgment, whereby inferences about other animals and situations may be affected by irrelevant information or emotional states.
Cognitive biology is an emerging science that regards natural [cognition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cognition) as a [biological function](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biological_function).

term: Cognitive clarity theory of learning to read
page: Cognitive clarity theory of learning to read

definition: Cognitive complexity describes [cognition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cognition) along a simplicity-complexity axis.
Cognitive description is a term used in psychology to describe the cognitive workings of the human mind.

Cognitive development is a field of study in [neuroscience](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuroscience) and [psychology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Psychology) focusing on a child's development in terms of information processing, conceptual resources, perceptual skill, language learning, and other aspects of the developed adult brain and [cognitive psychology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cognitive_psychology).
Cognitive discourse analysis (CODA) is a research method which examines natural language data in order to gain insights into patterns in (verbalisable) thought.
Cognitive ecology is the study of cognitive phenomena within social and natural contexts.
Cognitive ecology of religion is an integrative approach to studying how [religious beliefs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Religion) covary with social and natural dynamics of the environment.

Cognitive emotional behavioral therapy (CEBT) is an extended version of [cognitive behavioral therapy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cognitive_behavioral_therapy) (CBT) aimed at helping individuals to evaluate the basis of their emotional distress and thus reduce the need for associated dysfunctional [coping](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coping_(psychology)) behaviors (e.g., eating behaviors including binging, purging, restriction of food intake, and substance misuse).
Cognitive geography is an interdisciplinary study of [cognitive science](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cognitive_science) and [geography](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geography).

Cognitive inertia is the tendency – for a particular [orientation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orientation_(mental)) in an individual's thinking about a matter, belief, or strategy – to resist change.

Cognitive inhibition refers to the mind's ability to tune out [stimuli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stimulus_(physiology)) that are irrelevant to the task/process at hand or to the mind's current state.
cognitive load is the effort being used in the [working memory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Working_memory).

cognitive map is a type of [mental representation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mental_representation) used by an individual to order their personal store of information about their everyday or metaphorical spatial environment, and the relationship of its component parts.

cognitive module in [cognitive psychology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cognitive_psychology) is a specialized tool or sub-unit that can be used by other parts to resolve [cognitive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cognitive) tasks.

Cognitive musicology is a branch of [cognitive science](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cognitive_science) concerned with [[Cognitive model#Computational models|computationally modeling]] musical knowledge with the goal of understanding both music and cognition.

cognitive opening is a concept in social movement theory defined as a moment in which a catalytic event, sometimes a personal crisis or socioeconomic pressure, makes a person receptive to new ways of thinking because life changes challenge previously accepted beliefs, prompting a re-assessment of world views.

Cognitive poetics is a school of [literary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Literary) criticism that applies the principles of [cognitive science](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cognitive_science), particularly [cognitive psychology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cognitive_psychology), to the interpretation of literary [texts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Writing).

Cognitive polyphasia describes the condition in which different systems of knowledge or belief, possessing different rationalities, are held by an [individual](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Individual) or [collective](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Collective).

Cognitive psychology is the scientific study of human [mental process](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cognition)es such as [attention](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Attention), language use, [memory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Memory), [perception](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perception), problem solving, [creativity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Creativity), and [reason](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reason)ing.
Cognitive reframing is a psychological technique that consists of identifying and then changing the way situations, experiences, events, ideas and emotions are viewed.

Cognitive resource theory (CRT) is a [leadership](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leadership) theory of [industrial and organisational psychology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Industrial_and_organizational_psychology) developed by [Fred Fiedler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fred_Fiedler) and Joe Garcia in 1987 as a reconceptualisation of the [Fiedler contingency model](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fiedler_contingency_model).

cognitive revolution was an intellectual movement that began in the 1950s as an interdisciplinary study of the mind and its processes, from which emerged a new field known as [cognitive science](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cognitive_science).

Cognitive rigor is a combined model developed by superimposing two existing models for describing [rigor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rigour) that are widely accepted in the [education](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Educators) system in the [United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States).

page: Cognitive science of new religious movements
definition: Cognitive science of new religious movements is the study of [new religious movement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_religious_movement)s (NRMs) from the perspective of [cognitive science](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cognitive_science).
Cognitive science of religion is the study of religious thought, theory, and behavior from the perspective of the [cognitive science](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cognitive_science)s.

Cognitive Science Society is a [professional society](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Professional_society) for the [interdisciplinary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interdisciplinary) field of [cognitive science](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cognitive_science).

Cognitive specialization suggests that certain behaviors, often in the domain of social communication, are passed on to offspring and refined to be maximally beneficial by the process of natural selection.

[Cognitive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cognitive) strategies are the specific methods that people use to [solve problems](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Problem_solving) and/or exploit opportunities, including all sorts of reasoning, planning, arithmetic, etc.

Cognitive style or thinking style is a concept used in [cognitive psychology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cognitive_psychology) to describe the way individuals [think](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thought), perceive and remember information.

Cognitive tempo (a term of [cognitive psychology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cognitive_psychology), also known as reflectivity/impulsivity) is a type of [cognitive style](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cognitive_style) defined as the extent to which an individual differs in terms of their ability to respond carefully and slowly, as opposed to quickly and with errors.

Cognitive tests are assessments of the [cognitive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cognitive) capabilities of [human](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human)s and other [animal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Animal)s.
Cognitive Theory of Inquiry Teaching, also referred to as the Cognitive Theory of Interactive Teaching, was developed by Allan Collins and Albert L.

cognitive tradeoff hypothesis argues that in the cognitive [evolution of humans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evolution_of_humans), there was an [evolutionary tradeoff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evolutionary_tradeoff) between short-term working memory and complex language skills.

cognitive tutor is a particular kind of [intelligent tutoring system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intelligent_tutoring_system) that utilizes a [cognitive model](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cognitive_model) to provide feedback to [student](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Student)s as they are working through problems.

cognitive vulnerability in [cognitive psychology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cognitive_psychology) is an erroneous belief, [cognitive bias](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cognitive_bias), or pattern of thought that predisposes an individual to psychological problems.
Cognitive warfare consists of any military activities designed to affect attitudes and behaviors.
Cognitive-experiential self-theory (CEST) is a dual-process model of perception developed by [Seymour Epstein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seymour_Epstein).
cognitivism is a theoretical framework for understanding the mind that gained credence in the 1950s.

Cogstate Brief Battery (CBB) is a computer-based [cognitive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cognitive_neuroscience) assessment used in [clinical trial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clinical_trial)s, healthcare, and academic research to measure [neurological](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neurological) cognition.

Coherence therapy is a system of [psychotherapy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Psychotherapy) based in the theory that symptoms of [mood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mood_(psychology)), [thought](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thought) and [behavior](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Behavior) are produced coherently according to the person's current mental models of reality, most of which are implicit and unconscious.

term: Cold and heat adaptations in humans
page: Cold and heat adaptations in humans
definition: Cold and heat adaptations in humans are a part of the broad adaptability of [Homo sapiens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homo_sapiens).

collective action problem or social dilemma is a situation in which all individuals would be better off cooperating but fail to do so because of conflicting interests between individuals that discourage joint action.
Collective consciousness, collective conscience, or collective conscious () is the set of shared beliefs, ideas, and moral attitudes which operate as a unifying force within society.
Collective effervescence is a sociological concept coined by [Émile Durkheim](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Émile_Durkheim).
Collective identity or group identity is a shared sense of [belonging](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belongingness) to a [group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_group).

collective unconsciousness () is a term coined by [Carl Jung](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carl_Jung), referring to the belief that the [unconscious mind](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unconscious_mind) comprises the [instinct](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Instinct)s of [Jungian archetypes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jungian_archetypes)—innate symbols understood from birth in all humans.

collusion in couples' relations with two partners is a psychological term for behavioral patterns in relationships for couples therapy.

Communication Disorders Quarterly is a quarterly [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer_review) [academic journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academic_journal) that covers research on typical and atypical communication, from oral [language development](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Language_development) to [literacy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Literacy) in clinical and educational settings.

Communication quotient (CQ; alternately called communication intelligence or CI) is the [theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Business_philosophy) that [communication](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Communication) is a [behavior](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Behaviour)-based skill that can be measured and trained.

Comparative cognition is the comparative study of the mechanisms and origins of [cognition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cognition) in various [species](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Species), and is sometimes seen as more general than, or similar to, [comparative psychology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comparative_psychology).

Comparative Cognition Society (CCS) is one of the primary scientific societies for the study of [animal cognition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Animal_cognition) and [comparative psychology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comparative_psychology).
categories: Psychology organizations based in the United States

definition: Comparative psychology is the [scientific](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific) study of the [behavior](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Behavior) and [mental process](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mental_process)es of non-[human](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human) [animal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Animal)s, especially as these relate to the [phylogenetic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phylogenetic) history, [adaptive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adaptation) significance, and development of behavior.
comparator hypothesis is a psychological model of associative learning and performance.

term: Comparisons between Israel and Nazi Germany
page: Comparisons between Israel and Nazi Germany

definition: Compassion fade is the tendency to experience a decrease in [empathy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Empathy) as the number of people in need of aid increase.
Compassion fatigue is an evolving concept in the field of [traumatology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Traumatology).

compensation is a strategy whereby one covers up, [consciously](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Consciousness) or unconsciously, weaknesses, [frustration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frustration)s, desires, or feelings of inadequacy or incompetence in one life area through the gratification or (drive towards) excellence in another area.
competency evaluation is a means of determining the language proficiency of an individual without the requirement for [standardized testing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Standardized_test).
competency evaluation is an assessment of the ability of a [defendant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Defendant) to understand and rationally participate in a court process.

complex is a structure in the [unconscious](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unconscious_mind) that is [objectified](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Objectification) as an underlying [theme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theme_(narrative))—like a [power](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Power_(social_and_political)) or a [status](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_status)—by grouping clusters of [emotion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emotion)s, memories, perceptions and [wishes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wish_fulfillment) in response to a threat to the stability of the self.

Computational cognition (sometimes referred to as computational cognitive science or computational psychology or cognitive simulation) is the study of the [computation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computation)al basis of [learning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Education) and [inference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inference) by [mathematical model](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathematical_model)ing, [computer simulation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer_simulation), and [behavioral](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Behaviorism) experiments.

Computational linguistics is an [interdisciplinary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interdisciplinarity) field concerned with the [computational modelling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computational_modelling) of [natural language](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natural_language), as well as the study of appropriate computational approaches to linguistic questions.

Computational neuroaesthetics is the discipline that connects [neuroscience](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuroscience), psychology and [computer science](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer_science).

Computational neurogenetic modeling (CNGM) is concerned with the study and development of dynamic [neuronal models](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuronal_modeling) for modeling brain functions with respect to [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene)s and dynamic interactions between genes.

Computational semiotics is an interdisciplinary field that applies, conducts, and draws on research in [logic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Logic), [mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathematics), the [theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theory_of_computation) and [practice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer_programming) of [computation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer_science), [formal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Formal_language) and [natural](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natural_language) [language studies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linguistics), the [cognitive science](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cognitive_science)s generally, and [semiotics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Semiotics) proper.

computational theory of mind (CTM), also known as computationalism, is a family of views that hold that the human [mind](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mind) is an information processing system and that cognition and consciousness together are a form of [computation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computation).

Computational representational understanding of mind (CRUM) is a [hypothesis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hypothesis) in [cognitive science](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cognitive_science) which proposes that thinking is performed by [computations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computations) operating on representations.

definition: Computer-based test interpretation (CBTI) programs are technological tools that have been commonly used to interpret data in [psychological assessments](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Psychological_evaluation) since the 1960s.

Computers are social actors (CASA) is a [paradigm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paradigm) which states that humans unthinkingly apply the same social [heuristics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heuristics) used for human interactions to [computer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer)s, because they call to mind similar social attributes as humans.
Comrey Personality Scales (also known as Comrey Personality Test or CPT) is a [personality test](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Personality_test) developed by [[Andrew L.

Concealed ovulation or hidden estrus is the lack of any perceptible change (e.g., a change in appearance or scent) when an adult female is fertile and near [ovulation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ovulation).

definition: Concept creep (also known as semantic creep) is the process by which harm-related topics experience [semantic expansion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extension_(semantics)) to include topics which would not have originally been envisaged to be included under that label.

Concept learning, also known as category learning, concept attainment, and concept formation, is defined by [Bruner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerome_Bruner), Goodnow, he studied the computational basis of human learning and inference using behavioral testing of adults, children, and machines from Bayesian statistics and probability theory, but also from geometry, graph theory, and linear algebra.

conceptual metaphor, or cognitive metaphor, is the understanding of one idea, or [conceptual domain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conceptual_framework), in terms of another.
Concert abuse is a phenomenon attributed to the loss of [concert etiquette](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Concert_etiquette) between audience and performer.

Concord Prison Experiment, conducted from 1961 to 1963, was designed to evaluate whether the experiences produced by the psychoactive drug [psilocybin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Psilocybin), derived from [psilocybin mushrooms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Psilocybin_mushrooms), combined with [psychotherapy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Psychotherapy), could inspire prisoners to leave their [antisocial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Psychopathy) lifestyles behind once they were released.

Concreteness training (CNT) is the repeated practice of [cognitive skills](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cognitive_skill) to create [habitual behaviors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Habit) in order to help reduce anxiety and depressive symptoms for those suffering from the disorder of depression.
condensation () is when a single idea (an image, memory, or thought) or dream object stands for several associations and ideas.

Condescension or condescendence is a form of [incivility](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Incivility) wherein the speaker displays an attitude of patronizing superiority or [contempt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Contempt).

conditioned avoidance response (CAR) test, also known as the active avoidance test, is an [animal test](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Animal_model) used to identify [drug](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drug)s with [antipsychotic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antipsychotic)-like effects by checking if they limit the animals' will.
Conductive pedagogy is pedagogy especially useful for disabled pupils like those with [cerebral palsy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cerebral_palsy).
Confidence is the feeling of [belief](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belief) or [trust](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trust_(social_science)) that a person or thing is reliable.

Confidence weighting (CW) is concerned with measuring two variables: (1) what a respondent believes is a correct answer to a question and (2) what degree of certainty the respondent has toward the correctness of this belief.
Confined environment psychology is a refined subcategory of environmental psychology.

conflict procedure is an experiment often used in [scientific research](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_research) to quantify [anxiety](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anxiety) levels by measuring changes in punished/unpunished responses.
conflict style inventory is a written tool for gaining insight into how people respond to [conflict](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_conflict).

Congruence bias is the tendency of people to over-rely on testing their initial [hypothesis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hypothesis) (the most congruent one) while neglecting to test alternative hypotheses.

connectedness to nature scale (CNS) is a measure of individuals' trait levels of feeling emotionally connected to the natural world in the realm of [social](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_psychology) and [environmental psychology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Environmental_psychology).

Connectionism is an approach to the study of human mental processes and cognition that utilizes mathematical models known as connectionist networks or [artificial neural network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artificial_neural_network)s.

Connors form (also spelled Conners form or Conner's form) is a colloquial term used in [clinical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clinical_psychology) and [school settings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/School_psychology) for the [questionnaire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Questionnaire)s that make up the Conners [rating scale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rating_scale)s, multi-informant behavior rating instruments commonly used to assess symptoms of [ADHD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Attention_deficit_hyperactivity_disorder) and related difficulties in children and [adolescent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adolescent)s.
Connor–Davidson Resilience Scale (CD-RISC) was developed by Kathryn M.

conscience is a [cognitive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cognition) process that elicits [emotion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emotion) and rational associations based on an individual's [moral philosophy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethics) or value system.
Conscientiousness is the [personality trait](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Personality_trait) of being responsible, [[:wikt:careful|careful]], or [[:wikt:diligent|diligent]].
Consciousness is being aware of something internal to one's self, or of states or objects in one's external environment.

Conservation refers to a [logical thinking](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Logical_thinking) ability that allows a person to determine that a certain quantity will remain the same despite adjustment of the container, shape, or apparent size, according to the [psychologist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Psychologist) [Jean Piaget](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jean_Piaget).

Conservation of Resources (COR) Theory is a [stress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Psychological_stress) theory that describes the motivation driving humans to both maintain their current resources and to pursue new resources.

Conservation psychology is the scientific study of the reciprocal relationships between [human](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human)s and the rest of [nature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nature), with a particular focus on how to encourage [conservation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conservation_movement) of the [natural world](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natural_environment).

consideration of future consequences (CFC) is a [personality trait](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Personality_trait) defined as the extent to which individuals consider the potential future outcomes of their current behaviour and the extent to which they are influenced by the imagined outcomes.
Consoling touch is a pro-social behavior involving physical contact between a distressed individual and a caregiver.
consonance and dissonance are categorizations of simultaneous or successive [sound](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sound)s.

Conspicuous conservation describes [consumers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Consumer) who purchase [environmentally friendly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Environmentally_friendly) products in order to signal a higher [social status](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_status).

Constance Muriel Davey (4 December 1882 – 4 December 1963) was an Australian psychologist who worked in the [South Australia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Australia)n Department of Education, where she introduced the state's first [special education](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special_education) classes.
categories: Fellows of the British Psychological Society

definition: construal is a way that people perceive, comprehend, and interpret their world, particularly the acts of others toward them.

[Cognitive behavioral therapy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cognitive_behavioral_therapy) (CBT) is a [psychotherapeutic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Psychotherapy) approach that addresses dysfunctional emotions, maladaptive behaviors and cognitive processes and contents through a number of [goal-oriented](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goal-oriented), explicit systematic procedures.
